legislation.cert_required: UL or equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory
legislation.notes: H.B. 340 (2025) amends 54-15-102 and enacts 54-15-601. A 'portable solar generation device' HAS A MAXIMUM POWER OUTPUT OF NOT MORE THAN 1,200 WATTS, connects through a standard 120-volt AC outlet, meets the most recent National Electrical Code and is certified by UL or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory. It is expressly excluded from the definition of 'customer generation system', so net metering does not apply to it.

watt_tiers.effect: Exempt from the interconnection requirements of 54-15-106 and from an interconnection agreement under 54-15-103; not subject to net metering. The electrical corporation may not require approval, charge a fee, or demand extra equipment.

certification_requirement.quote: is certified by Underwriters Laboratories or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory
certification_requirement.note: Verbatim from the primary text. 'Nationally recognized testing laboratory' is the term used in 29 C.F.R. 1910.7; UL, CSA and Intertek/ETL are all NRTLs. A CE mark is a European self-declaration and is not an NRTL listing.
